data.title: Sandisk slides 13% on post-earnings selloff
data.description:
Shares of Sandisk Corporation (SNDK), a standalone NAND flash memory and storage company, sank more than 13% on Friday after the firm's fiscal first-quarter earnings report.

The stock closed at $1,150.89, down $179.16 on the day. Investors weighed strong datacenter demand and a surprise stock split against lingering concerns over consumer weakness and competitive pressures in the memory market.

What Happened to Sandisk

The session's decline followed Sandisk's fiscal first-quarter earnings release on October 29, which showed results and guidance above analyst estimates. The company reported non-GAAP diluted earnings of $49.51 per share and revenue of $11.03 billion for the quarter, beating consensus estimates.

For the second quarter, management guided revenue to a range of $12.2 billion to $12.6 billion and non-GAAP earnings to $55 to $57 per share on a pre-split basis.

Along with the results, Sandisk's board approved an 8-for-1 forward stock split. Shareholders of record on November 9, 2026 are set to receive seven additional shares for each share held, with split-adjusted trading expected to begin on November 20, 2026.

On the earnings call, management emphasized AI-driven NAND demand, datacenter mix expansion, and the growing adoption of New Business Model agreements as the predominant way Sandisk works with customers. The company also pointed to substantial adjusted free cash flow generated in the quarter.

On the negative side, management acknowledged that consumer revenue declined sequentially as customers adjusted to higher pricing, while wafer production lead times limit the company's ability to reallocate supply quickly.

data.title: American Savings Bank signals NIM expansion as it expects one Fed rate hike in Q4 2026
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: American Savings Bank (ASBH) Q3 2026

Management View

  • “We appreciate you joining us for our first earnings call as a public company.” (President, CEO & Director Ann Teranishi)
  • “We delivered another quarter of strong earnings with net income of $29 million or $0.45 per diluted share, return on average assets of 1.29% and a return on average tangible common equity of 16.68%.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Average loan balances increased and deposit costs decreased despite a rising rate environment.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Local economists continue to forecast growth in 2026, but have recently lowered their estimates.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Net interest income was $76.4 million, up $1.2 million from the prior quarter... Net interest margin was 3.61%, 4 basis points higher than the prior quarter and 15 basis points higher than the prior year period.” (Executive VP & CFO Dane Teruya)
  • “With our ability to generate capital and our focus on returning capital to shareholders, the Board declared a quarterly dividend of $0.27 per common share payable on November 20 to shareholders of record as of November 9.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Nonperforming loans were 29 basis points of total loans compared with 19 basis points in the prior quarter... net charge-offs were $1.8 million or 11 basis points on an annualized basis.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Steven Nakahara)

Outlook

  • “What you'll see is it slightly ticking up in the fourth quarter, but relatively only about a couple of basis points up.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Right now, we're expecting one [rate hike] in the fourth quarter. There is also probably a couple that will occur in 2027... we would expect our cost of funds to inch higher as those rate changes become effective.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Our balance sheet continues to be neutral to slightly asset sensitive, which will support NIM expansion in this higher for longer interest rate environment.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “For this year, we think that the effective tax rate will be closer to 22%... the tax rate in the mid-22s to 23% level is an appropriate level going forward.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “With this rate environment, we are expecting the residential portfolio to stay flat... production will really offset the runoff.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)

Financial Results

  • “Net income for the third quarter was $29 million, an increase of $1.8 million or 6.7% from the prior quarter.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Noninterest income was $21 million, down $2.8 million from the prior quarter, primarily due to lower fair market value adjustments related to our BOLI portfolio.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Noninterest expense was $59 million, down $2.1 million from the prior quarter, primarily due to lower fair market value adjustment related to our deferred compensation plan.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Total assets were $8.9 billion at quarter end, down $112.2 million or 1.2% from June 30.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Total deposits ended the quarter at $8.1 billion, down $137.6 million or 1.7% from the prior quarter... Noninterest-bearing deposits made up 31.5% of total deposits.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “Our Tier 1 leverage ratio increased to 9.24% and our total capital ratio increased to 14.76%.” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya)
  • “The allowance for credit losses on loans was $60.2 million at quarter end or 97 basis points of total loans... Provision expense was $0.7 million in the third quarter, down $2.6 million from the linked quarter.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara)

Q&A

  • Jeff Rulis, D.A. Davidson: asked about deposit-cost pressure and margin trajectory; Executive VP & CFO Teruya replied, “what you'll see is it slightly ticking up in the fourth quarter... only about a couple of basis points up,” and added, “we would expect our cost of funds to inch higher as those rate changes become effective.”
  • Jeff Rulis, D.A. Davidson: asked about the expense run-rate excluding one-time fair value items; Executive VP & CFO Teruya said, “if you eliminate the fair market value related to our deferred comp plans, we think the -- that would be a good run rate for the fourth quarter,” and noted “some inflationary impacts on that number.”
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked about reinvestment opportunities from single-family runoff and securities cash flows; Executive VP & CFO Teruya said, “The cash flow that came off in the third quarter was roughly about $55 million,” and added, “we got roughly about $74 million runoff... reinvesting... at a spread of a little more than 175 basis points.”
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked about CD runoff and new CD duration; Executive VP & CFO Teruya responded, “our customers' demand is going to be a little shorter... promotional campaigns in the 3-month and 6-month range,” and said, “we think that trend will continue, but eventually will stabilize.”
  • Matthew Clark, Piper Sandler: asked about timing for a buyback; Executive VP & CFO Teruya replied, “we haven't made any determination on what we're going to be doing with that excess capital, but we're having active discussions.”
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: asked about deposit outflows and early Q4 trends; Executive VP & CFO Teruya answered, “The deposit outflow in the third quarter was seasonal,” and added, “we do expect a pickup in the fourth quarter.”
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: asked about the nonaccrual increase and interest income impact; Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara said, “The increase in nonaccrual was associated with the partial charge-off of the same CRE construction deal,” and added, “no material change on the interest income.”
  • Andrew Terrell, Stephens: asked about the go-forward tax rate; Executive VP & CFO Teruya said, “the tax rate in the mid-22s to 23% level is an appropriate level going forward.”
  • Kelly Motta, KBW: asked about the loan pipeline and growth outlook; President, CEO & Director Teranishi replied, “The pipeline is looking pretty steady and healthy, not as robust as earlier this year,” and added, “we're really being disciplined in our approach on credit as well as pricing.”
  • Kelly Motta, KBW: asked about momentum in noninterest-bearing deposits; President, CEO & Director Teranishi said, “we continue to have a terrific steady deposit base,” while Executive VP & CFO Teruya added, “We're really trying to build primary banking relationships.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was neutral to slightly skeptical, concentrated on rate sensitivity, deposit behavior, expense run-rate, and capital return, including buyback timing.
  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and largely steady in Q&A, emphasizing consistency and discipline, including “Our balance sheet continues to be neutral to slightly asset sensitive” (Executive VP & CFO Teruya) and “we're really being disciplined in our approach on credit as well as pricing” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi).
  • A prior-quarter transcript was not provided, so tone changes versus last quarter were not discussed on this call.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The previous-quarter transcript was not available in the provided materials, so changes in strategy, guidance language, and tone versus last quarter could not be directly assessed.

Risks and Concerns

  • “Local economists continue to forecast growth in 2026, but have recently lowered their estimates.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “Hawaii faces elevated oil prices and impacts from recent storms.” (President, CEO & Director Teranishi)
  • “In the third quarter, we recognized a partial charge-off of a nonperforming commercial construction loan.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara)
  • “Nonperforming loans were 29 basis points of total loans compared with 19 basis points in the prior quarter.” (Executive VP & Chief Credit Officer Nakahara)

Final Takeaway

American Savings Bank framed Q3 as a strong quarter marked by net income of $29 million and modest net interest margin expansion, while management highlighted a low deposit-cost profile and a “neutral to slightly asset sensitive” balance sheet positioned for incremental NIM improvement in a “higher for longer” rate backdrop. In Q&A, management’s near-term focus centered on limited deposit-rate pressure (“only about a couple of basis points”), seasonal deposit flows expected to reverse in Q4, disciplined loan growth with a flatter residential outlook, and ongoing Board discussions about optimizing capital beyond the newly declared $0.27 quarterly dividend, alongside continued monitoring of credit performance following a partial charge-off that lifted nonaccruals.

data.title: WisdomTree outlines plan to launch 15 to 20 Atlantic House products over 18 to 24 months as Onchain platform expands partnerships
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: WisdomTree (WT) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Our assets under management reached a record $171 billion at quarter end, marking our seventh consecutive quarter of record AUM." (Chief Financial Officer Bryan Edmiston) "During the quarter, we generated $4.6 billion of net inflows, with positive contributions across the firm, including $2.4 billion in the U.S., $1.7 billion in Europe, and $500 million from onchain." (CFO Edmiston)

  • "We also remained active on capital management, retiring the remaining $18 million principal amount of our 2029 convertible notes using cash while repurchasing approximately $11 million of common stock during the quarter, representing roughly 500,000 shares." (CFO Edmiston)

  • "We have launched our first two products in Europe, leveraging the team's capabilities, with plans to launch 15 to 20 products over the next 18 to 24 months." (President & COO Robert Lilien) "With Ceres, we launched Fund II in mid-June and already have a strong pipeline with more than $100 million of potential demand from over 100 investors in the mid to late stages." (President & COO Lilien)

  • "We have been embedding AI into workflows across the firm for several years now, not as a headcount reduction initiative." (President & COO Lilien) "In 2026, we have tracked more than 1,500 hours saved per month through AI, the equivalent of at least 10 full-time employees." (President & COO Lilien)

  • "We announced recently, bringing our digital asset initiatives together under one name, WisdomTree OnChain." (Head of Digital Assets William Peck) "We have a novel tokenized ETF proposal in front of the SEC today." (Head of Digital Assets Peck) "We have recently announced relationships with firms globally, including BitGo, MoonPay, Stable Sea, Hashkey, Marketnode, and Synthesys." (Head of Digital Assets Peck)

  • "In 2027, we expect to bring private market allocations into the ETF wrapper." (Founder, CEO & Director Jonathan Steinberg) "I believe tokenization will fundamentally change how financial assets are issued, distributed, and traded." (CEO Steinberg)

Outlook

  • "We are updating our full-year guidance to range from $83 million to $87 million" for discretionary spending, "reflecting a modest $2 million reduction to the high end of our previous range." (CFO Edmiston)

  • "We are also narrowing our 3rd party distribution guidance to $21 million to $23 million." (CFO Edmiston) "Our interest income guidance is increased by $1 million to $9 million." (CFO Edmiston)

  • "We expect 4th quarter diluted shares to range from 154 million to 160 million shares, including incremental shares associated with our convertible notes, at an average stock price of $21 to $24 per share." (CFO Edmiston)

  • On strategy timing, management reiterated a 2027 window for private assets in ETFs: "we expect this to be a 2027 event." (CEO Steinberg)

Financial Results

  • "Revenues were $179.4 million during the quarter, an increase of 1% from the 2nd quarter." (CFO Edmiston) "Adjusted operating margins were 43.1% for the quarter" and "Adjusted net income for the quarter was $49.5 million, or $0.32 per share." (CFO Edmiston)

  • On the revenue mix and variability, "Revenues were $179.4 million" was "partly offset by lower transaction fees from our European ETPs and lower performance fees." (CFO Edmiston)

Q&A

  • Wilma Jackson Burdis, Raymond James & Associates, Inc., Research Division: "You just mentioned the ability to bring privately held companies to an ETF format... we'd love to hear more"; Founder, CEO & Director Steinberg: "we are not sharing right now specific fund mechanics or the launch dates beyond that we expect this to be a 2027 event."

  • Burdis, Raymond James & Associates, Inc., Research Division: "expense growth seemed to moderate this quarter"; Chief Financial Officer Edmiston: "Some of that seasonality over the summer months, some of that's just continuing to control our spend, and some of that is just realizing further leverage in our comp ratio as well."

  • Burdis, Raymond James & Associates, Inc., Research Division: "the profitability of the tokenization business"; Head of Digital Assets Peck: "this business is very much in investment mode today, so we don't disclose kind of separate financials"; CEO Steinberg: "Bryan has given guidance that we are spending sort of the mid-20s from an operating loss standpoint."

  • George Sutton, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, Research Division: "some of those edges that you have built"; Head of Digital Assets Peck cited in-sourcing regulated infrastructure: "own its own transfer agent," "regulated trust company," and "FINRA-member broker-dealer"; CEO Steinberg: "our ability to move quickly, be responsive... I think shows up in these partnerships."

  • Sutton, Craig-Hallum Capital Group LLC, Research Division: "how big can this tokenized money market fund alone be"; Head of Digital Assets Peck: "it could be a huge fund" and pointed to "about $8 trillion in money market funds, $16 trillion in ETFs."

  • Michael Cyprys, Morgan Stanley, Research Division: "how are you thinking about the opportunity to translate all of that growth there into meaningful revenue and earnings"; Head of Digital Assets Peck: "expense ratio" and "services that the broker-dealer could provide"; CEO Steinberg added a third lever: "net interest income from greater stablecoin usage."

  • Cyprys, Morgan Stanley, Research Division: on the "Binance hack"; Head of Digital Assets Peck: "major stablecoin issuers actually froze their stablecoins" and "it wouldn't really even be possible to do with our money market fund... given how we do the transfer restrictions."

  • John Coffey (for Chris), Oppenheimer & Co. Inc., Research Division: on "tokenization as a service"; Head of Digital Assets Peck: "There are active conversations regarding it today" and "we think our tokenization as a service offering could play a really important role"; CEO Steinberg: it could help "demonstrate the inherent value in the investments that we have made in the platform."

  • Mike Grondahl, Northland Capital Markets, Research Division: on ETF platform fees; CFO Edmiston: "these 3rd party distribution fees, they are roughly 3% of our total revenue" and "there shouldn't be a material deviation from this ratio going into next year"; President & COO Lilien: "Distribution economics have been part of what we do for years."

  • Grondahl, Northland Capital Markets, Research Division: on models growth; Global Chief Investment Officer Jeremy Schwartz: "custom models in the U.S. have been really gaining a lot of traction" and "Atlantic House has also added reach to our models and solutions business."

  • Aditya Sharma (for Alex), Goldman Sachs Group, Inc., Research Division: on the SEC innovation exemption; Head of Digital Assets Peck: "We are very confident in our model of having the fund issue shares directly Onchain" and "that model is fully supported within the innovation exemption as well."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts: slightly positive but probing on monetization, platform fees, and security, including "how are you thinking about the opportunity to translate all of that growth there into meaningful revenue and earnings" (Cyprys, Morgan Stanley) and "what you think this dynamic looks like" on platform fees (Grondahl, Northland).

  • Management: positive and expansion-oriented in prepared remarks ("WisdomTree continues to execute exceptionally well" (CEO Steinberg)) and more guarded on specifics in Q&A ("I don't think I can say more about that at this time" (CEO Steinberg) on private assets in ETFs).

  • Versus last quarter, valuation language stayed prominent, but Q3 added more emphasis on distribution execution and near-term partnerships; CEO Steinberg said in Q3, "The delta here between what's in our stock today and what should be realized, I think is quite immense," while in Q2 he said, "we believe our own platform... is largely unrecognized in our current valuation." (CEO Steinberg)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Record AUM and inflow momentum accelerated: Q3 "record $171 billion" and "$4.6 billion of net inflows" (CFO Edmiston) vs. Q2 "$162.9 billion" and "$3.1 billion of net inflows" (CFO Edmiston).

  • Guidance adjustments shifted: Q3 raised "interest income guidance" to "$9 million" and tightened discretionary spend to "$83 million to $87 million" (CFO Edmiston), while Q2 lowered interest income to "$8 million from $10 million" tied to buybacks (CFO Edmiston).

  • Share count guidance widened upward in Q3: "4th quarter diluted shares" of "154 million to 160 million" (CFO Edmiston) vs. Q2 guidance of "152 million to 155 million" for the second half (CFO Edmiston).

  • Strategic narrative broadened: Q3 highlighted an AI-driven strategy where "one of our AI-driven long-short strategies... has outperformed the market by more than 900 basis points so far this year" (CEO Steinberg) and reiterated private-market ETF plans: "In 2027, we expect to bring private market allocations into the ETF wrapper." (CEO Steinberg)

Risks and Concerns

  • Tokenization economics remained an investment: "this business is very much in investment mode today" (Head of Digital Assets Peck) and management referenced "mid-20s" operating loss guidance for Onchain (CEO Steinberg).

  • Regulatory uncertainty persisted despite a constructive tone: "while the CLARITY Act stalled in the Senate, adoption of stablecoins and tokenized securities has continued." (Head of Digital Assets Peck)

  • Revenue sensitivity to market activity was reiterated: Q3 revenue growth was "partly offset by lower transaction fees from our European ETPs and lower performance fees." (CFO Edmiston)

Final Takeaway

WisdomTree’s Q3 message centered on scaling a record AUM base with continued broad inflows, tightening elements of expense-related guidance, and leaning into three growth pillars that management framed as increasingly connected: liquid alternatives expansion through Atlantic House product launches, private-market exposure in ETF wrappers targeted for 2027, and Onchain distribution via newly announced partnerships and a tokenized ETF proposal, while acknowledging the digital assets build remains in an investment phase.

data.title: Origin Agritech gets Nasdaq notice over $1 minimum bid price rule
data.description:
• Origin Agritech (SEED) announced Friday that it received a Nasdaq notice for failing to meet the $1 minimum bid price requirement after its shares closed below the threshold for 30 consecutive business days.
  • The company has until April 26, 2027, to regain compliance by maintaining a closing bid price of at least $1 for 10 consecutive business days.
  • Its shares will continue trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market during the compliance period.
  • The company may qualify for an additional 180-day extension and could consider a reverse stock split to regain compliance.
  • Source: Press Release

data.title: Spooky end of the month for stocks? SA analyst sees a bull run into year-end
data.description:
Seeking Alpha analyst Alex King of Cestrian Capital Research believes the stock market will see a much desired runup by the end of the year.

“We are calling for a bull run in equities into year-end,” King said.

Despite the ongoing equity selloff, led by semiconductors and the overall artificial intelligence-adjacent sector, King said market conditions are ripe for a rally.

U.S. Treasury yields (US10Y), (US2Y), (US30Y), and the U.S. dollar (DXY) are on the wane, while high-beta assets, such as cryptocurrencies, “are proving resilient in times of stress.”

The 10-year Treasury yield (US10Y) is 4.93%, while the 2-year Treasury yield (US2Y) is 4.59%. The 30-year Treasury yield (US30Y) is 5.31%.

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) has declined 7.6% in the past month, and it is trading at around $76,850.

The S&P 500 (SP500) finished -1.8%, while the Nasdaq Composite (COMP:IND) closed -2.9%, and the Dow (DJI) ended -1.1%.

“Even today’s 3% drop in the Nasdaq (COMP:IND) held up and is over the critical 200-day moving average,” he added. “Ignore sentiment; focus on price."

data.title: State Department approves $2.1B Patriot missile sale to Ukraine
data.description:
The U.S. State Department said Friday it approved the sale of as many as 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles, as well as spare parts, logistics, and support, to Ukraine for $2.1B.

Lockheed Martin (LMT) is the principal contractor for the ‌sale; in July, the U.S. Army awarded the company a contract ​worth up to $58.6B to produce ⁠Patriot interceptor missiles.

The PAC-3 is the most advanced Patriot missile; it uses "hit-to-kill" kinetic energy - colliding directly with targets at over Mach 5 - rather than a blast fragmentation warhead, featuring a dual-pulse solid rocket motor and larger fins for extended range and maneuverability against ballistic and hypersonic threats, according to the Lockheed Martin (LMT) website.

Ukraine will pay for the Patriot order with "donations from Canada, Germany, and Norway via the JUMPSTART program and national funds, financed by the European Union’s Ukraine Support Loan," and no U.S. funds are involved in the sale, the State Department said.

Ukraine's President ​Zelenskyy said earlier this week that his country had been waiting for nearly a month ​for the U.S. to sign off on critical missile supplies, as Russia stepped up attacks on energy and civilian infrastructure.

data.title: Nasdaq tanks 5% in October as tech bloodbath deepens
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index (COMP:IND) plummeted nearly 3% on Friday amid a wider selloff in the technology sector, intensified by Intel’s (INTC) weak third-quarter results.

The tech-heavy index closed 2.86% lower at 25,437 points, recording its worst single-day performance since June.

Intel’s shares nosedived during Friday’s trading session, closing 29.38% lower after its Q3 results showed guidance that missed Wall Street estimates by a considerable margin. Its peers Sandisk (SNDK) and Qualcomm (QCOM) also took a hit, ending 13.42% and 11.12% lower, respectively.

For the week, Nasdaq slumped 2.79%, while for the month, it tanked 5.30%.

The index closed lower in 11 of October’s 21 trading sessions, capping a volatile month that began with the Nasdaq notching record highs. Investor sentiment swung between concerns over rising AI capital expenditure and optimism following the Federal Reserve’s dovish stance on interest rates. Meanwhile, intermittent selling across the tech sector intensified towards month-end following disappointing results from Big Tech companies like Alphabet (GGOG) (GOOGL) and Amazon (AMZN).

Top five gainers of the month:

Roper Technology (ROP) +28.69%

Regeneron Pharmaceutica (REGN) +26.28%

Intuit (INTU) +20.62%

GE HealthCare (GEHC) +19.68%

data.title: Capri signals fiscal 2027 EPS of $2.20 on ~$3.42B revenue as Michael Kors targets return to growth in Q4
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Capri Holdings Limited (CPRI) Q2 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • "We are encouraged by the momentum build at both Michael Kors and Jimmy Choo" (Chairman & CEO John Idol), adding that "new fall product introductions are generating some of the strongest full price sell-throughs we have seen in years" and that management is "increasing our fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings per share guidance" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Revenue was impacted by approximately $50 million due to inventory delays, which constrained product availability" at Michael Kors (Chairman & CEO Idol), while the company continued to push "approximately 40% less markdown inventory" and "reduced promotional activity by approximately 50%" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Today, we have 7 Jet Set lounges" and "we have renovated 50 stores as we advance toward our goal of renovating 300 stores" (Chairman & CEO Idol), while also stating, "next year, we're going to open between 50 and 75 brand-new stores" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Second quarter revenue exceeded our expectations, increasing 11.5% over last year" at Jimmy Choo (Chairman & CEO Idol), and management said it "continue[s] to expect Jimmy Choo to return to profitability in fiscal 2027" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • "Total company revenue of $809 million decreased 5.5% on a reported basis" and "net income was $45 million or $0.42 per diluted share versus a loss per share of $0.03 last year" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Tyler Reddien).

Outlook

  • "We now anticipate fiscal 2027 revenue of approximately $3.42 billion" and "expect to generate diluted earnings per share of $2.20" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), while also raising the capital return assumption: "we now anticipate weighted average shares outstanding of approximately 108 million, reflecting share repurchases of $300 million during fiscal 2027" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • "Turning to third quarter guidance. We expect total company revenue of just over $1 billion" and "expect to generate diluted earnings per share of $0.95" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), noting the quarter includes "the impact of the $20 million of wholesale shipments that shifted from the third quarter into the second quarter" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • On what changed versus last quarter’s framing, management said the improved outlook was tied to in-quarter execution and brand momentum: "based on our second quarter performance and our expectations for the remainder of the year, we are increasing our fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings per share guidance" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Financial Results

  • "Total company operating income of $31 million represented operating margin expansion of 150 basis points year-over-year to 3.8%" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), while "gross margin of 63.3% increased 230 basis points versus last year" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • By brand, "Michael Kors revenue of $663 million decreased 8.6%" while "Jimmy Choo. Revenue of $146 million increased 11.5%" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), with each brand benefiting from shipment timing: "around $15 million" for Michael Kors and "approximately $5 million" for Jimmy Choo shifting from Q3 into Q2 (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Balance sheet and buybacks were a key investment focus: "we ended the second quarter with cash of $125 million and debt of $461 million, resulting in net debt of $336 million, down from $1.6 billion last year" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), and "repurchasing $150 million worth of shares" including "10.3 million shares" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

Q&A

  • Matthew Boss, JPMorgan: "could you speak to the drivers of sequential month-over-month improvement" and "support your confidence for positive revenue growth in the back half"; Chairman & CEO Idol: "we were very pleased" and said the business is "literally chasing inventory on certain products" while emphasizing promotions were "down by 50%" and inventory was "$50 million less than we had planned" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Brooke Roach, Goldman Sachs: asked about "Michael Kors Americas outlet" and "How quickly can you chase" winning products; Chairman & CEO Idol: outlet saw "slightly stronger acceleration" and on Hamilton Soft, "The sell-throughs, I would say, surprised us" and "we're moving as fast as we possibly can" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Simeon Siegel, Guggenheim: asked the "right size" of wholesale and back-half gross margin drivers; Chairman & CEO Idol: "somewhere in the 20% range, 25% range" for wholesale mix and "we believe is going to return to growth next year" (Chairman & CEO Idol). Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien: "we are expecting that we'll see a bit of a pullback in the expansion" in 2H gross margin, citing tariffs and anniversarying prior benefits (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Adrienne Yih-Tennant, Barclays: asked about a "fashion shift" and whether customers are "new" vs "reactivated"; Chairman & CEO Idol: "we are definitely seeing the fashion winds shift" and said, "we're attracting new younger customers" and that TikTok Shop is "almost 4x from what we had originally anticipated" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Rakesh Patel, Raymond James: asked about AUR durability as quality-of-sale moderates; Chairman & CEO Idol: "we've started to raise prices in outlet" and said more selective increases are planned because "they're not good enough. We have much higher aspirations" (Chairman & CEO Idol). Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien: "we do see significant opportunities in terms of gross margin expansion" beyond fiscal 2027 (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Mark Altschwager, Baird: asked whether Q3 assumes October trends hold and whether full-price turns positive; Chairman & CEO Idol: "there's absolutely a sequential improvement planned throughout the quarter" and "this does assume that Michael Kors full price does return to positive during the quarter" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly positive and validation-seeking, anchored on inflection points and durability, including: "It is really nice to see the gross margin inflection" (Adrienne Yih-Tennant, Barclays) and "It is really nice to see the gross margin inflection" themes repeated across outlets and AUR questions.

  • Management’s tone was positive in prepared remarks and confident in Q&A, frequently reinforcing momentum signals such as "these are more than just green shoots" (Chairman & CEO Idol) and framing capital return as conviction: "This increase underscores our confidence" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Versus last quarter’s more cautious framing around "headwinds" and a "disappointed" Q2 outlook, management now leaned more assertively on recovery language, including "we are increasing our fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings per share guidance" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance moved up from "fiscal '27 revenue of approximately $3.4 billion" and EPS "approximately $2.15" (Q1 call, Chairman & CEO Idol) to "fiscal 2027 revenue of approximately $3.42 billion" and EPS "$2.20" (Q2 call, Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • The assumed repurchase level increased from "share repurchases of $200 million during fiscal 2027" (Q1 call, Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien) to "share repurchases of $300 million during fiscal 2027" (Q2 call, Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

  • Operationally, Q1 emphasized "lower-than-anticipated inventory levels at Michael Kors in the second quarter" (Chairman & CEO Idol), while Q2 described improving flow and sell-throughs and said "the majority of these actions are now behind us" on quality-of-sale resets (Chairman & CEO Idol).

Risks and Concerns

  • Supply chain and availability remained a key risk: "Revenue was impacted by approximately $50 million due to inventory delays" (Chairman & CEO Idol), and management highlighted continued freight constraints: "issues with getting freight out of Asia" and "supplementing with air" (Chairman & CEO Idol).

  • Regional and macro risks were explicitly cited: EMEA was "impacted by the broader effects of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien), while margins face pressure as "second half tariff rates on average will be a bit higher" and the company anniversaries "the tariff refund" (Executive VP, CFO & COO Reddien).

Final Takeaway

Management characterized Q2 as a turning point where Michael Kors product newness and lower promotions drove improving monthly trends, while Jimmy Choo extended double-digit growth momentum. Leadership raised full-year guidance to approximately $3.42 billion in revenue and $2.20 in diluted EPS, paired with an increased $300 million share repurchase assumption, while continuing to flag inventory timing, tariffs, and Middle East-related demand pressures as the principal swing factors into the back half.

data.title: Reddit falls 29% to new 52-week low on weak Q4 guidance
data.description:
Reddit (RDDT) shares tumbled about 29% on Friday, closing at $91.73 after a drop of $37.87 on the day. The slide took the stock to a new 52-week low of $89.28.

The social platform reported third-quarter results that beat expectations but issued fourth-quarter guidance that came in below analyst consensus. 

Reddit reported Q3 revenue of $895 million, up 53% year over year, with GAAP EPS of $1.40. Despite those beats, management's Q4 revenue outlook of $1.0–$1.03 billion fell short of consensus, and warnings about deteriorating search-referral traffic sent shares sharply lower. data.title: Xponential Fitness jumps as investor looks to purchase Club Pilates owner (update)
data.description:
Update 4:48pm: Adds Fund 1 confirmation in filing.

Xponential Fitness (XPOF) soared 19% after Fund 1 Investments LLC, the third-largest holder,  said it was looking to buy the company,

Fund 1 is prepared to offer a price of $5.61 to $7 a share to purchase Xponential (XPOF), the owner of Club Pilates and Pure Barre brands,  according to a letter disclosed in a 13D/A filing on Friday.  At the top of the range, an offer would value XPOF at a premium of 87% to its closing price on Thursday.

Fund 1 owns almost 10% of Xponential's outstanding shares and has economic exposure to almost 20% of the company, according to the filing.

"While we are interested in acquiring 100% of the Company, we also are open to allowing other shareholders to participate in the acquisition alongside Fund 1, with Fund 1 acquiring the majority interest, so that they can take part in any upside," Fund 1 said in the letter to the Xponential board on Friday.

News of the offer was earlier reported by Bloomberg.

Xponential didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment from Bloomberg.

"Our interactions with the Board to date have been highly constructive, and we are grateful to you for that,"  Fund 1 wrote in the letter. "We came into this situation with an open mind and, given the governance challenges the Company has faced in the past, expected hurdles. Instead, we have been genuinely, positively surprised." 

In April, Xponential (XPOF), the franchisor of boutique fitness studios, announced that its board has initiated a review of strategic alternatives to maximize shareholder value.
